title: Tabs
overview: Same-page panels under one view. One tablist; arrow keys; the selected tab owns the panel.
apply_when: Related views of the same object that must stay on one URL.
not_when: A nav of destinations (links), or a stepper (progress / task_list).

role.overview: Same-page panels under one view. One tablist; the selected tab owns the panel.
role.apply_when: Related views of the same object that must stay on one URL.
role.not_when: A nav of destinations (links), or a stepper (progress / task_list).

size.overview: Highest in the size hierarchy — the easiest to hit.
size.apply_when: The view's main instance, or full-width on a small viewport.
size.not_when: A dense toolbar or a third option next to the main control.

size.apply_when: Ordinary use in forms, pages, and chrome.
size.not_when: The only control on a mobile screen that should span the width.

size.overview: Lowest in the size hierarchy — densest.
size.apply_when: Inline or chrome that sits beside content.
size.not_when: The page's primary instance, or a control under 44×44.

composition.overview: Tabs in a tablist; panels are labeled by the selected tab.
composition.not_when: A row of links that change the URL (that is navigation).

state.not_when: A visual underline with no aria-selected.
Hidden panels still in the tab order.

state.overview: Keyboard is on a tab. Must stay visible.
state.apply_when: Arrows or Tab onto the tablist.

accessibility.overview: The set is a tablist; each tab names its panel.

keyboard.overview: Tab lands on the tablist, then into the selected panel — not every tab as a stop, unless the house uses automatic activation.
keyboard.not_when: Every tab is a stop and the panel is unreachable.

keyboard.overview: Enter (or automatic selection) shows the focused tab's panel.
keyboard.not_when: Enter follows a URL instead of switching panels.

keyboard.overview: Home/End jump to first/last tab when that is the house.
